notes.calculus-chapter-14-problems-plus-1-prob: The sum factors as[x²+(L−x)²][y²+(W−y)²]. Each factor is minimized at its midpoint and maximized at an endpoint. Genuine four positive-area rectangles require interior cuts, so the endpoint bound is a supremum.
notes.calculus-chapter-14-problems-plus-2-prob: The gradient is a positive scalar multiple of⟨−2x,−4y⟩. Its slope is2y/x, yielding y=Kx²; the arrows follow increasing concentration toward the origin.
notes.calculus-chapter-14-problems-plus-3-prob: The trapezoid area is x sinθ[w−2x+x cosθ]. Optimize in x and θ; the semicircle uses arc lengthπr=w.
notes.calculus-chapter-14-problems-plus-4-prob: |x+y+z|≤√3ρ bounds |f| by3^(r/2)ρ^(r−2). Along the x-axis, r≤2 cannot give limit0. Because x+y+z can be negative, arbitrary real exponents need a stated signed/absolute-power convention; the literal real-power formula on R³ excludes irrational and even-denominator exponents.
notes.calculus-chapter-14-problems-plus-5-prob: g_x=f(y/x)−(y/x)f′(y/x), g_y=f′(y/x). At any source point x≠0, Euler’s degree-one identity gives Z=g_x X+g_y Y, which passes through the origin.
notes.calculus-chapter-14-problems-plus-6-prob: Linearize both equations at the current point and solve the2×2 Jacobian system for the correction. The two positive intersections are symmetric under interchange of x,y; independently substituting the high-precision roots verifies both equations.
notes.calculus-chapter-14-problems-plus-7-prob: Set A=1/a²,B=1/b². Enclosure means max_(0≤y≤2)[2Ay+(B−A)y²]≤1. The optimum has B=A−A² and maximizes AB=A²(1−A), giving A=2/3,B=2/9, hence a=√(3/2),b=3/√2. The endpoint-contact branch cannot improve the area.
notes.calculus-chapter-14-problems-plus-8-prob: Cauchy–Schwarz for vectors(a,b,c) and(x,y,1) proves the bound. Equality requires proportional vectors. This exposes the omitted c=0 exception in the source claim; along(x,y)=t(a,b) the bound is approached as |t|→∞.
